summary: Stale hourly-tag led to missing invoice line for reserved+hosted hybrid batch embedding run
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that a large multi-region batch embedding job on 2026-03-08 was partially billed, with an entire hourly invoice line missing for ~2.5 hours of hosted fallback usage. The job ran on Storlium's dedicated pool with automatic fallback to hosted in eu-west due to transient capacity constraints. Impact: customer expects reserved-rate credits to apply for the reserved portion and a hosted line item for the fallback hours; instead the hosted fallback hours are missing from the invoice, resulting in an under-invoiced period and incorrect credit application. This has caused Storlium to report reconciliation gaps against their internal spend dashboard and they request an adjustment and explanation.
impact: Storlium Analytics reports a missing invoice line for ~2.5 hours of hosted fallback usage during a hybrid reserved-hosted job. Financial reconciliation gap of ~$1,200 and inability to map usage to forecasted reserved capacity - customer is enterprise/dedicated and flagged as P1.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer launches multi-region batch embedding job (job-id: stl-batch-20260308-09) pinned to reserved pool in us-east with fallback enabled.
2) At 2026-03-08T10:14:00Z reserved pool in eu-west reported saturated and smart routing routed 2.5 hours worth of microbatches to hosted nodes in eu-west.
3) Metering postbacks recorded hosted tokens for the fallback intervals and wrote hourly tags to the postback queue.

4) Reconciler run on 2026-03-09 consumed the postbacks but an hourly-tag value (hour_window_id) was set to a stale replication tag for that organisation and those hosted tokens were not emitted as a separate invoice line.
5) Customer checks invoice for March and cannot find any hosted line for 2026-03-08 10:00-12:30 window while reserved usage lines are present.
6) Customer provides usage export and account audit CSV to Support.
7) Support triggers manual re-recon and requests billing engine to re-run ledger generation for the affected hour.
Expected: for fallback-hosted usage to appear as a hosted invoice line and reserved credits to remain applied to reserved hours.
logs_and_artifacts: Customer-provided artifacts: usage_export_storlium_20260308.csv, job_manifest_stl-batch-20260308-09.json, hosted_postback_samples.log. Server-side artifacts: reconciler log snippet (reconciler-2026-03-09-03.log lines 4832-4855), hourly-tag index dump for org 88a2 (hour_index_88a2-20260308.dump), billing_ledger_partial_202603-report.json. Error observed in reconciler log: 'WARN reconciler: hour_tag mismatch for org=88a2 hour=2026-03-08T10:00:00Z expected_tag=2026030810 current_tag=2026030709'.

investigation_notes: Initial triage: reconciler emitted warning about hour_tag mismatch; postbacks for affected interval ingested but grouped under stale hour index, causing ledger generator to drop group during invoice-line emission step.

Hypothesis: race between postback-indexer replication and reconciler consumer left a stale hour_tag value in cache for org 88a2. When ledger job grouped by hour_window_id it saw a tag from the previous day and excluded it due to dedup guard (to prevent double-billing).

Evidence: reconciler log shows 'expected_tag != current_tag' and the hourly index dump contains two different hour_window_id entries for the same token batch; postback timestamps match the hosted fallback period.

Repro attempt: reprocessing the exact postback batch through a local reconciler replayer yields proper emission of invoice line when hour_tag is fixed to the correct value; when left stale the line is omitted.

Scope: initial scan shows only this org and one other small customer had similar pattern in the same time window; likely related to a replication lag event in the indexer on 2026-03-08 09:58-10:20 UTC.
Risk assessment: low likelihood of broad account impact but medium severity for affected customers due to billing correctness.
root_cause: A stale hour_tag value in the hourly index for org 88a2 (Storlium) caused the postbacks from hosted fallback microbatches to be grouped under a tag that the ledger emitter considered already-processed. The deduplication guard therefore suppressed emission of a hosted invoice line for the affected hour window.
resolution_summary: Billing team performed a manual ledger re-run for the affected hours and emitted a credit memo for the missing hosted fallback usage. A manual invoice adjustment will be visible on Storlium's billing dashboard and a credit memo email sent by 2026-03-16. Reconciler and indexer teams deployed a hotfix to ensure the postback-indexer updates hour_tag atomically and added an alert for hour_tag replication lag above 1 minute.
resolution_steps_taken: 1) Applied manual patch to hourly index to correct hour_window_id entries for org 88a2.
2) Re-ran reconciler ledger generation for 2026-03-08 10:00-12:30 window in a staging-run and validated emitted invoice lines matched customer usage export.
3) Generated and issued credit memo CR-2026-00347 for $1,203.40 covering hosted fallback hours; invoice adjusted and customer notified via billing@example.redwood.com.
4) Deployed reconciler/indexer hotfix (PRs: reconciler#412, metering#209) to write hour_tag updates atomically and backfill missing tags for last 48 hours on startup.
5) Created monitoring alert 'hour_tag_replication_lag' to page SRE for >60s lag and added a runbook to reprocess affected postbacks.
6) Follow-up: schedule a postmortem and notify finance to confirm invoice reconciliation with customer on 2026-03-16.
resolution: Credit memo created and invoice adjusted. Hotfix deployed to prevent recurrence. Customer will receive confirmation and credit details by 2026-03-16.
next_steps: 1) Finance to confirm credit memo application and close out with Storlium (owner: Diego Martinez, due 2026-03-16).
2) Postmortem and RCA doc to be published to Confluence and linked here (owner: SRE lead, due 2026-03-20).
3) Expand hourly-tag replication test in CI to include high-ingest microbatch scenarios (owner: metering team).
4) Outreach to the second affected customer for disclosure and remediation steps.
5) Close ticket after customer confirms credit receipt and accounting matches their reconciliation.

A hotfix prevents the replication lag that caused the omission; we'll follow up with documentation and the postmortem. If you need the credit applied to your next invoice or as a refund, please confirm and we'll arrange it.
